title: THE DEACON KNOCKS BACK
description: A production made only from one printed record: THE VELVET HEARSE, "The Deacon Is Dead" (1972, imaginary), a funeral home played as a band in seven equal steps. Slowed two of its own steps to 96 BPM, rebuilt from one-shots, with the Deacon answering every knock from inside.

tracks.description: Lucius's likembe alone (the record's thumb section and pickup), seven equal steps, the bed under the wake.
Iggy's three knocks on the lid, as found, as a neutral triad, as the coffin's seven-step scale; an octave above the record (R1).
The Deacon's knock from inside at 0.552 of its speed: the tonic an octave under the bass, saturated so a phone hears it; also his three knocks before the drop, as recorded.
The urn: one palm thud from the break.
The rosary-bead snare: one slap and one ghost tap from the break, laid back.
One shake of the collection plate, on every sixteenth.
The hearse spring tried once on the tonic, played as a new bass line in seven equal steps, with glides.
Odile's friction drum: squeaks, a moan, a laugh that stutters.
The record as found: two bars of Odile, the seven steps cut to half-bars, the hot shout, the last bar.
The preparation-room door: opening at half speed, lifting at half speed, closing.
